prompt: Challenge C144-CH2: Downstream purification — specifically the ultrafiltration step — runs at only 55% of nominal throughput because the membranes foul with res

content.text: {"claims":[{"claim":1,"text":"Cross-flow ultrafiltration with spiral-wound polyethersulfone membranes experiences irreversible fouling that reduces flux within hours of operation, with irreversible fouling after 8 h quantified at 18 % flux loss; a two-step cleaning sequence (0.3 % citric acid, then 0.5 % NaOH) restored 94 % of clean-water flux.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-07419","field":"abstract","quote":"Irreversible fouling after 8 h was quantified at 18 % flux loss; a two-step cleaning sequence (0.3 % citric acid, then 0.5 % NaOH) restored 94 % of clean-water flux."}]},{"claim":2,"text":"The critical flux concept can be applied to map stable operating windows for oil filtration, and cross-flow microfiltration is discussed with reference to fouling mechanisms, critical flux, and membrane selection.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-07415","field":"abstract","quote":"The critical flux concept was applied to map stable operating windows for this oil type."},{"id":"SYN-PUB-07417","field":"abstract","quote":"Cross-flow microfiltration of crude and partially refined oils is discussed with reference to fouling mechanisms, critical flux, and membrane selection."}]}]}
